chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I heard him saying: 'Do not trim your hair when you intend to perform Hajj in Dhi al-Qadah, nor in the month in which you intend to perform Umrah.'

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةَ: Umrah, the minor pilgrimage to Mecca.
key_terms.تَأْخُذْ مِنْ شَعْرِكَ: Trim/take from your hair, referring to the cutting or removal of hair which is prohibited during Ihram.
key_terms.ذِي الْقَعْدَةِ: Dhi al-Qadah, the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, one of the four sacred months.

ai.seo_question: When does the prohibition of trimming hair begin for someone intending to perform Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific timing of the hair-trimming prohibition, distinguishing between the general sacred months of Hajj (Dhi al-Qadah) and the specific month designated for Umrah. It highlights the scholarly distinction in Shia fiqh regarding when the state of Ihram restrictions formally begins for these pilgrimages, emphasizing the sanctity of the sacred months as outlined in the Quran.
